data.narrative:
Exowatt is a Series A climate and energy technology company founded by Hannan Happi and Jack Abraham that has raised $90M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 9 companies in the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though direct same-stage comparables within this narrow peer set are limited.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable framework here. Using total capital raised of $90M as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, this method yields an implied valuation of $180M. A peer-median approach was not viable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data points within the Climate & Energy sector; a broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $153M to $207M, with a median point of $180M. This range reflects moderate sensitivity around the stage-progression step-up assumption. Key uncertainties center on the scarcity of tightly matched private peer valuation data at this stage and the heterogeneity of business models and capital intensity across the Climate & Energy sector. Any refinement would require either additional comparable exits or disclosed financing rounds at proximate stages.
